title: Pretérito perfecto compuesto: lo que los Estados han logrado

sections.content: The present perfect (han emprendido, han profesionalizado, han creado) connects a past process to its continuing relevance now -- the natural tense for describing an institutional trend that started decades ago and is still shaping the state you're reading about. These sentences are taken directly from the previous reading.

items.spanish: Los Estados latinoamericanos han emprendido un proceso de fortalecimiento institucional que contrasta con la debilidad crónica del siglo diecinueve.
items.english: Latin American states have undertaken a process of institutional strengthening that contrasts with nineteenth-century chronic weakness.

items.spanish: Los gobiernos han profesionalizado sus ejércitos, sustituyendo las antiguas montoneras por fuerzas armadas nacionales.
items.english: Governments have professionalized their armies, replacing the old irregular militias with national armed forces.

items.spanish: Muchos gobiernos han creado, por primera vez, sistemas de recaudación de impuestos relativamente eficaces.
items.english: Many governments have created, for the first time, relatively effective tax-collection systems.

items.spanish: Este Estado ha dejado de limitarse a la capital para extenderse hacia el resto del territorio nacional.
items.english: This state has stopped limiting itself to the capital, extending instead toward the rest of the national territory.

sections.content: Ha dejado de + infinitive (has stopped doing something) is a common present-perfect pattern worth learning as a chunk -- dejar de always signals the end of a habitual action, not a single completed event.
